searchText: Previously at Scroll we've had issues of some geth-generated witnesses missing entries required by revm (though we might be using outdated implementations). Is the purpose of the execution witness standardization to eliminate these differences? BAL should clarify those cases, and make witnesses canonical. For [example](https://github.com/bluealloy/revm/issues/3484) geth previously included system call, but it got [fixed few](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/33977) weeks ago. Revm for example had loaded all access list items, this is not a case any more. Thanks! In our case the most recent discrepancy was that revm expected to read the delegated code, even if the call failed on the balance check: https://github.com/scroll-tech/go-ethereum/pull/1277/changes yep exactly -- there is a canonical execution witness that is "minimal" Oh this is interesting. Didnt know about it. Even if balance transfer is zero we still need to make target account (and delegate) warm and warming is essentially loading of accont to evm journal. So for this one imo it makes sense. Happy to triage if there are more cases. BAL did clear a lot of them. Ignacio triaged some of them [here](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/22289) by running against an earlier version of the execution witness specs. The newer version that we released from the execution specs repo also has tests for edge cases, so it probably makes sense to use that I think And this one https://github.com/paradigmxyz/stateless/pull/8 too :)
